payload.brief: Create a software to turn my Markdown notes into a searchable static site with tags and backlinks.
payload.problem_statement: User needs a way to convert personal Markdown notes into a browsable, searchable static website that supports tag-based organization and bidirectional linking between notes.
goals: G1: Generate a static site from Markdown files that can be hosted without a backend server
G2: Implement full-text search functionality across all notes
G3: Support tag-based categorization and filtering of notes
G4: Automatically detect and render backlinks between notes
G5: Preserve Markdown formatting and structure in the generated site
non_goals: NG1: Real-time collaborative editing of notes
NG2: Dynamic server-side rendering or database integration
NG4: Version control or history tracking of note changes
NG5: Authentication or access control features

constraints.text: Output must be static HTML/CSS/JS that can be hosted on any web server or CDN
Must process standard Markdown format as input

assumptions.text: User has Markdown notes stored locally in files
Backlinks follow wiki-style [[note-name]] or similar syntax
Tags are embedded in Markdown files using a consistent format (e.g., frontmatter or inline #tags)
User wants to self-host or use static hosting (GitHub Pages, Netlify, etc.)
Search can be client-side JavaScript-based rather than requiring a search server
User has basic command-line or build tool familiarity for running the generator

open_questions.text: What specific Markdown flavor/extensions should be supported (CommonMark, GFM, etc.)?
What is the expected scale (number of notes, total size)?
What syntax should be used for backlinks and tags?
Should the site support themes or customizable styling?
Are there any specific search features required (fuzzy search, filters, sorting)?
Should the tool watch for file changes and auto-regenerate, or run on-demand only?
What platforms/operating systems must be supported?

success_metrics: SM1: Successfully generates static site from 100+ test Markdown files within 10 seconds
SM2: Search returns relevant results within 200ms for typical queries
SM3: All backlinks are correctly identified and rendered as clickable links
SM4: Tag pages correctly aggregate all notes with each tag
SM5: Generated site loads and functions in modern browsers (Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Edge) without errors
stakeholders: Potential future users with similar note-taking workflows

glossary.definition: A website consisting of fixed HTML, CSS, and JavaScript files that do not require server-side processing
A bidirectional reference between notes, showing which other notes link to the current note
A lightweight markup language with plain text formatting syntax
A keyword or label used to categorize and organize notes by topic or theme
